judged_text: The Salesforce refresh is hard-coded as an unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com in the service constructor and is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens like every other integration in this diff, so the feature silently does not cover Salesforce. Self-hosters using credential sync get Salesforce refreshing against the provider endpoint with local app keys that may not exist on their instance (this is the exact scenario the feature exists for); additionally the network call now fires on every service construction even when the stored access token is still valid, and the `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is fragile under HTTP/2 (statusText is empty) so valid responses will be rejected with a 400.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor now unconditionally performs a refresh fetch to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and updates the credential before returning a `jsforce.Connection` (see the new `const response = await fetch(...)` block right after `const credentialKey = ...`). This refresh path is not routed through the newly added `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (unlike the other integrations in this diff), so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will still hit the provider token endpoint instead of the sync endpoint, undermining the feature’s intended coverage. Additionally, the error check `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is fragile and can reject valid responses (better to use `response.ok` / `response.status`), making this a correctness bug grounded in the shown code.
